page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmg5s.24xlarge is an ECS Bare Metal family server based on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs. Memory capacity stands at 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exact ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance operates without bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware.

Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 32 Gbps, accommodating high-throughput data transfer between cloud infrastructure endpoints. Because the server features zero local disk storage, persistent data and root volumes rely entirely on external network-attached block storage. The underlying bare metal design provides dedicated processor execution without hypervisor resource contention, though management integrates with Alibaba Cloud virtualization infrastructure.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the balanced 1:4 processor-to-memory allocation provides resource density suitable for non-specialized horizontal scaling and enterprise application consolidation. The absence of local solid-state storage eliminates overhead costs for ephemeral disks when remote block storage is already standard architecture. Workloads aligning with this instance include distributed microservices, enterprise enterprise resource planning backends, mid-sized database management systems, and high-concurrency web serving tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmg5s.24xlarge is an ECS Bare Metal instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for disk operations, nor does it feature GPU acceleration. Network interfaces provide a baseline throughput of 32 Gbps for sustained traffic. With its bare metal compute density and dedicated CPU allocation, this configuration suits medium-to-large database hosts, general enterprise applications, high-traffic web backends, and container orchestration clusters requiring balanced processor and memory allocations.
